programme.title: Parcours B1 — 21 h
programme.subtitle: Communiquer dans des situations professionnelles courantes
programme.public_target: Salariés, demandeurs d'emploi, indépendants devant utiliser l'anglais dans des situations professionnelles courantes (accueil, administration, logistique, services, qualité, assistanat).
programme.prerequisites: Niveau A2 minimum à l'entrée, vérifié par le test de positionnement de la plateforme (prérequis de validation de la fiche RS6905). Ordinateur ou tablette avec micro et casque, connexion internet stable.
objectives: Se présenter et décrire son poste, son entreprise et ses missions à l'oral en 45 à 90 secondes de façon structurée (C3).
Comprendre les informations générales et au moins deux détails précis d'une conversation professionnelle courante (C1).
Identifier l'objet, la demande, l'échéance et le ton d'un email ou d'un document professionnel courant (C2).
Participer à une réunion simple : donner son avis, demander une précision, reformuler (C1, C3).
Rédiger en 30 minutes un email ou un compte rendu structuré d'au moins 150 mots (C4).
programme.modalities: Formation ouverte et à distance (FOAD) : e-learning asynchrone sur la plateforme (leçons, audio, exercices auto-corrigés, studio oral, atelier d'écriture) et classes virtuelles synchrones avec le formateur.
programme.accompaniment: Formateur référent joignable par la messagerie de la plateforme (réponse sous 48 h ouvrées), rendez-vous individuels réservables dans l'agenda, assistance technique par messagerie (catégorie « support technique »).
programme.means: Plateforme LMS accessible 24 h/24, ressources audio et PDF téléchargeables, formateur anglophone qualifié (CV et compétences tenus à jour dans la plateforme).
programme.evaluation: Positionnement d'entrée ; exercices auto-corrigés et productions corrigées par le formateur ; quiz de fin de module (seuil 70 %) ; simulation d'entraînement aux 4 compétences ; évaluation finale interne ; questionnaires de satisfaction à chaud et à froid. Passage de la certification VTest sur la plateforme officielle d'ExAssess.
programme.accessibility: Formation accessible aux personnes en situation de handicap : demande d'aménagement confidentielle dès la candidature, analysée par le référent handicap (police agrandie, contrastes, temps majorés en entraînement, sous-titres et transcriptions). Les aménagements de l'examen officiel relèvent du certificateur.

modules.titre: Se présenter et décrire son activité
objectifs: À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de se présenter à l'oral en 45 à 60 secondes en citant au moins son poste, son service et deux responsabilités.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de décrire son entreprise (secteur, taille, clients, outils) en 60 à 90 secondes avec au moins trois informations chiffrées ou concrètes.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de poser au moins quatre questions correctement formées pour faire connaissance avec un interlocuteur et de restituer sa présentation à la 3e personne.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de rédiger en 30 minutes un email de présentation d'au moins 150 mots comportant objet, salutation, présentation, objet de la prise de contact, proposition de suite et formule finale.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'identifier la consigne ou l'information principale d'une annonce professionnelle de 10 à 20 secondes (au moins 3 réponses justes sur 4).
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de noter sans erreur un nom épelé, un numéro de téléphone, une date et une référence entendus dans un appel ou un message vocal.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'identifier le lieu, le problème et l'action suivante dans un dialogue court entre collègues.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de repérer l'information générale et au moins deux détails précis d'une réunion ou d'un briefing de 1 à 3 minutes.

modules.titre: Lire des emails et documents professionnels
objectifs: À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'identifier l'objet, la demande, l'échéance et le ton d'un email professionnel de 120 à 300 mots en répondant correctement à au moins 70 % des questions.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de repérer dans une note de service, un mémo ou un avis la mesure annoncée, les personnes concernées et les actions attendues.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'extraire d'une offre, d'un bon de commande, d'une brochure ou de conditions de vente les prix, délais, conditions et exceptions pertinents.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de distinguer dans un article ou un compte rendu les faits, les arguments et le point de vue de l'auteur.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de choisir entre lecture globale (skimming) et recherche ciblée (scanning) pour répondre à des questions dans un temps limité.

modules.titre: Participer à des échanges et réunions simples
objectifs: À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'identifier l'objectif, les points de l'ordre du jour et les décisions d'une réunion enregistrée de 1 à 2 minutes en répondant correctement à au moins 70 % des questions.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'exprimer en 45 à 90 secondes une opinion structurée (position + 2 raisons) et un désaccord poli assorti d'une proposition alternative.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de poser au moins deux questions de clarification et de reformuler correctement une consigne reçue à l'oral.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'ouvrir et de conduire un point d'équipe de 5 minutes en annonçant l'objectif, le déroulé en étapes et les attendus de chaque participant.

modules.titre: Rédiger des emails et comptes rendus
objectifs: À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de rédiger en 30 minutes un email professionnel de 150 mots minimum comportant objet, salutation, raison du message, demande ou réponse structurée, action attendue avec échéance et formule finale adaptée au destinataire.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'utiliser au moins six mots de liaison différents (addition, contraste, cause, conséquence, séquence, conclusion) correctement ponctués dans un texte de 150 mots.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de rédiger un document préparatoire à une réunion présentant objectifs, points de l'ordre du jour avec responsable et durée, préparation demandée et résultats attendus.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de rédiger un compte rendu ou un retour d'expérience distinguant faits, décisions et actions (qui, quoi, quand) avec les temps du passé appropriés.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de répondre en temps limité à des questions sur des énoncés, dialogues courts et longs, monologues et messages, en repérant le message général et au moins deux détails précis.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'identifier l'objet, la demande, l'échéance et la position de l'auteur dans un email, une note et un article (au moins 7 questions sur 9).
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de lire à voix haute trois textes, de répéter six énoncés et de répondre à deux questions ouvertes en utilisant au moins 80 % du temps de parole prévu.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de rédiger en 30 minutes un email structuré de 150 mots minimum, puis de formuler trois objectifs de préparation à partir de son autoévaluation.

competences: C1 — Écouter et comprendre un ensemble d'énoncés, de dialogues et de monologues en anglais afin de repérer, distinguer, identifier, sélectionner et apprécier des informations qui permettent de valider le degré de compréhension de la langue anglaise parlée nécessaire dans un contexte professionnel.

C2 — Comprendre et analyser un ensemble de textes, emails et articles en anglais afin de repérer, distinguer, identifier, sélectionner et apprécier des informations qui permettent de répondre à des questions avec précision dans un contexte professionnel.
C3 — S'exprimer et communiquer à l'oral en anglais afin d'apprécier les aptitudes à échanger, décrire, formuler, argumenter sur un ensemble de sujets dans un contexte professionnel.

C4 — Rédiger en anglais avec un vocabulaire et des tournures grammaticales appropriées afin de mesurer les aptitudes à écrire, décrire, formuler, questionner, argumenter, structurer ses idées sur un sujet donné dans un contexte professionnel.

syntheseHtml:
• Parcours B1 (21 h) préparant au VTest Business English – 4 Skills (RS6905, Répertoire spécifique, certificateur EXASSESS, enregistrement du 28/11/2024 au 28/11/2027) ; le test est passé en ligne sur la plateforme VTest, l'organisme assure la préparation.
• Les 4 compétences du référentiel sont travaillées : C1 — Écouter et comprendre un ensemble d'énoncés, de dialogues et de monologues en anglais ; C2 — Comprendre et analyser un ensemble de textes, emails et articles en anglais ; C3 — S'exprimer et communiquer à l'oral en anglais ; C4 — Rédiger en anglais avec un vocabulaire et des tournures grammaticales appropriées.
• 6 modules (29 leçons) : cours, langue clé, vocabulaire, dialogues, exercices auto-corrigés, studio oral et atelier d'écriture corrigés par le formateur, quiz de validation à 70 %.
• Le niveau A2 du CECRL est le minimum requis pour valider la certification : le test de positionnement d'entrée oriente vers le parcours adapté.
adaptationsHtml:
• Niveau de départ fixé par le test de positionnement ; le parcours peut être complété par les leçons du niveau inférieur ou supérieur.
• Rythme libre en e-learning, réécoute des audios et reprise des exercices ; classes virtuelles pour l'oral.
• Transcriptions et traductions disponibles pour chaque dialogue.
• Situation de handicap : le référent handicap étudie les aménagements (police agrandie, contrastes, temps majorés en entraînement, sous-titres) ; les aménagements de l'examen officiel relèvent du certificateur.
• Les sujets d'expression orale et écrite peuvent être rapprochés du poste du stagiaire.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Imani Brooks: Morning, everyone. This will only take five minutes. From next Monday, all incoming post will be opened and scanned by the mail room, and you'll receive it electronically instead of on paper. / Imani Brooks: The aim is to stop letters getting lost between floors, which happened three times last month. / Imani Brooks: So, what do I need from you? Please check the shared mailbox twice a day, once in the morning and once after lunch, and move each letter to the right case folder. / Imani Brooks: Original documents will be kept in the mail room for three months, so you don't need to print anything. If you have questions, send them to me by Friday. » — What does Imani ask the team to do?
options: Keep original documents for three months
Check the shared mailbox twice a day
Send her a report every Friday
questions.explication: « Please check the shared mailbox twice a day ». Les originaux sont conservés par le service courrier, pas par l'équipe, et il n'est pas nécessaire d'imprimer.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Project coordinator: Hi Mr Adams, thanks for joining. I'd like to give you an update on the installation of your new heating system. / Client: Thanks. Is everything on schedule? We need the offices to be warm before the staff move in. / Project coordinator: Mostly, yes. But one of the parts we ordered from Germany is delayed by about ten days. / Client: Sorry, did you say ten days or two days? / Project coordinator: Ten, I'm afraid. One-zero. / Client: So what you're saying is that the system won't be ready for the move on the first of November? / Project coordinator: Not completely. But we can install temporary electric heaters on the ground floor, where most of your staff will work, at no extra cost. / Client: OK, that sounds reasonable. Could you send me the new timetable in writing? / Project coordinator: Of course. You'll have it by tomorrow morning. » — What is the problem with the project?
options: The client wants to change the heating system.
A part will arrive about ten days late.
The staff have already moved in.
The installation will cost more than planned.
questions.explication: « one of the parts… is delayed by about ten days », confirmé par « Ten… One-zero ». « two days » est la mauvaise compréhension que le client vérifie.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Sven Lindgren: OK, everyone, let's make this quick. We have a customer audit next Thursday, and the purpose of this briefing is to make sure we're ready for it. / Sven Lindgren: I'll do three things. First, I'll remind you which areas the auditor will visit. Then, I'll show you the new checklist. And finally, I'll explain what I need from each of you. / Sven Lindgren: So, here's what I expect. Each of you is responsible for your own area. Please use the checklist to check it, and send me photos of anything that needs fixing by Wednesday at noon. / Sven Lindgren: You won't need to work overtime for this, and you won't need to meet the auditor unless she asks you a question directly. Any questions, ask me after the briefing. Thanks. » — What is each team member expected to do?
options: Work extra hours before Thursday's audit
Check their area and send photos of problems
Meet the auditor on Thursday morning
Write a report on the new checklist by Wednesday
questions.explication: « Please use the checklist to check it, and send me photos… by Wednesday at noon ». Rencontrer l'auditrice n'est nécessaire que si elle pose une question directe.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Kenji Watanabe: Hi, I'm Kenji. I look after our key accounts in the Asia region, so I travel to Singapore quite often. » — What is Kenji's job mainly about?
questions.explication: « look after our key accounts » = suivre les clients importants. Il voyage souvent, mais l'organisation de voyages n'est pas son métier.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Helen Visser: Our head office is in Leeds, but most of our sixty engineers work on customer sites across the north of England. » — Where do most of the engineers work?
options: At the head office in Leeds
questions.explication: « most of our sixty engineers work on customer sites ». Leeds est le siège, où travaillent peu d'ingénieurs.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Building manager: Please note that the car park will be closed on Saturday for cleaning. Staff working at the weekend can park at the sports centre next door. » — Where should weekend staff park on Saturday?
questions.explication: « Staff working at the weekend can park at the sports centre next door. » Le parking habituel est fermé pour nettoyage.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Team leader: When a customer returns a product, check the receipt first. You don't need to call a manager unless the product is more than thirty days old. » — When should staff call a manager?
options: If the product is older than 30 days
If the customer has lost their receipt
If the product was bought today
questions.explication: « You don't need to call a manager unless the product is more than thirty days old » : uniquement au-delà de 30 jours. « unless » = sauf si.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Supplier: Hello, it's Peter from Lumen Paper. Your order will arrive on Thursday instead of Tuesday, because our truck needs repairs. Sorry for the inconvenience. » — What is Peter calling about?
questions.explication: La livraison passe de mardi à jeudi : c'est un changement de jour. La commande n'est pas annulée.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Receptionist: Good morning, Mr Lee. Your meeting with Ms Clark has been moved to room 406, on the fourth floor. She'll join you there in about ten minutes. » — What has changed?
options: The person Mr Lee will meet
questions.explication: « has been moved to room 406 » : seule la salle change. Les « ten minutes » indiquent le délai avant l'arrivée de Ms Clark, pas un nouvel horaire.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Sales manager: We sold fifteen machines in March, which is good, but we'd planned fifty, so we really need to work harder this spring. » — How many machines did they sell in March?
questions.explication: « We sold fifteen machines » : accent sur la seconde syllabe (fif-TEEN). 50 était l'objectif prévu.

questions.question: Complétez les consignes de lecture stratégique avec le mot correct (vocabulaire vu en classe virtuelle) : « Before answering, _____ the document to understand the main topic. Then read the questions and scan the text for specific information. Remember that a second language may be an advantage but not essential. In the email, sessions take place in Ashford unless otherwise stated. Places are allocated in order of reply. »
questions.explication: Pour comprendre le thème général, on fait une lecture globale : « skim ».

questions.question: Document (email) : « From: Sofia Lindgren To: Digital Project Team Subject: Preparation – project review, Tuesday 9 April Dear all, Our mid-project review of the new customer portal will take place on Tuesday 9 April from 10:00 to 11:30 in Meeting Room 3 (a video link will be sent to remote participants). Objectives The aim of this meeting is to check progress against the plan, agree on how to deal with the delay on the payment module and confirm the date of the user tests. Agenda 1. Progress since the kick-off – Raj (15 min) 2. Payment module: options to recover the delay – Karen (30 min) 3. User tests: dates and volunteers – Sofia (20 min) 4. Budget update – Tom (15 min) 5. AOB (10 min) Expected outcomes By the end of the meeting, we should have a decision on the payment module and a confirmed test date. Preparation Please read Karen's two-page note on the payment module before Tuesday and come with your questions. If you cannot attend, let me know by Friday so that we can send you the minutes. Best regards, Sofia » — What must participants do before the meeting?
options: Read a note about the payment module
Send their questions to Karen by Friday
questions.explication: « Please read Karen's two-page note … before Tuesday ». Le piège « Send their questions by Friday » mélange deux informations : les questions sont à apporter en réunion, et le vendredi concerne seulement les absents.

questions.question: Document (email) : « From: Daniel Okafor <d.okafor@brentfield-eng.example> To: Events Team, Harbourline Hotel Subject: Group booking request – 14–16 May Dear Events Team, I am writing on behalf of Brentfield Engineering to ask about accommodation and a meeting room for our regional sales conference. We expect 22 participants, who will arrive on the evening of 14 May and leave after lunch on 16 May. We would need 22 single rooms for two nights, a meeting room for 25 people on 15 May from 9 am to 5 pm, and lunch for the group on both days. A projector and a flipchart would also be essential. Could you please send us a quotation, including your cancellation policy, by Friday 4 April? Our finance department needs to approve the budget before the end of next week, so we cannot wait longer than this. If you have any questions about our requirements, please contact my assistant, Leila Moreau, on 01632 960 418, as I will be travelling until Wednesday. Kind regards, Daniel Okafor Sales Operations Manager » — What is the main purpose of the email?
options: To confirm a booking that has already been made
To ask for a price for rooms and a meeting space
To complain about a previous conference at the hotel
questions.explication: « I am writing… to ask about accommodation and a meeting room » puis « Could you please send us a quotation » : il s'agit d'une demande de devis. L'option 0 est tentante car l'email est très détaillé, mais rien n'est encore réservé.

questions.question: Complétez ce point mensuel avec le mot de liaison qui correspond à la relation logique entre les idées : « Monthly update – Customer service team Response times improved in May. For example, the team answered 92% of emails within 24 hours, compared with 81% in April. This progress is mainly _____ the new ticketing tool, which sorts requests automatically. We have therefore decided to recruit a temporary assistant for the summer. Overall, the team is on the right track, but we need to keep an eye on the phone line. »
questions.explication: « due to » + nom (the new ticketing tool) exprime la cause. « because » doit être suivi d'un sujet et d'un verbe, ou de « because of ».

questions.question: Document (email (learner draft)) : « Learner draft – task: reply to a customer who complained about a late delivery (150 words minimum) Hi, I received your email. The delivery was late. The truck had a problem. The truck arrived on Tuesday. We are sorry. We will give you a discount. The discount is 10%. Send me your order number. Thanks Ryan » — Which version of sentences 2 to 4 is the most cohesive?
options: The delivery was late. The truck had a problem and the truck arrived on Tuesday.
Although the delivery was late, the truck had a problem on Tuesday.
The delivery was late because our truck broke down, so it only arrived on Tuesday.
The delivery was late, however the truck had a problem, so arrived on Tuesday.
questions.explication: « because » donne la cause, « so » la conséquence, et « it » évite la répétition de « the truck ». La version avec « Although » crée un contraste illogique, et la dernière utilise « however » après une virgule sans sujet ensuite.

questions.question: Choisissez le mot de liaison adapté : « _____ the heavy traffic, the delivery arrived on time. »
questions.explication: « the heavy traffic » est un groupe nominal : il faut « Despite ». « Although » exigerait un sujet et un verbe (Although the traffic was heavy).

questions.question: Choisissez le verbe introducteur correct pour un compte rendu : « At the meeting, Mr Chen _____ that the marketing budget should be reduced. »
questions.explication: « suggest that + sujet + should/verbe » est correct. « told » exige un complément de personne (told us that) et « agreed to » est suivi d'une base verbale.

questionsOuvertesDebut.question: Describe a problem you had at work. What happened, what did you do to solve it, and what did you learn from it?
questionsOuvertesDebut.reponseAttendue: Last year, I was responsible for organising a training day for twenty new employees. Two days before the event, the trainer called me to say she was ill and couldn't come. At first I panicked, because the programme was already printed and everyone had booked the day. So I contacted two experienced colleagues, and they agreed to run the morning session. Then I asked the training company to send a replacement for the afternoon, and they found someone the same day. In the end, the feedback was very positive. What I learned is that you should always have a plan B, so now I keep a list of internal colleagues who can step in at short notice.

questionsOuvertesDebut.question: Your team is moving to a new office next month. Write an email to your colleagues to explain the move. Include: the date and the new address, what they need to do before the move, and what will be different in the new office. (Rappel : écrivez un courriel structuré à vos collègues, au moins 150 mots, en traitant les trois points demandés.)
questionsOuvertesDebut.reponseAttendue:
Subject: Our move to the new office on 14 November

Hi everyone,

As you know, our team is moving to a new office next month. I'd like to give you some practical information so that the move goes smoothly.

The move will take place on Friday 14 November. From Monday 17 November, we will work at 25 Harbour Street, on the fourth floor. The building is a ten-minute walk from Central Station, and there is a car park behind it.

Before the move, please do three things. First, clear your desk and put your personal items in the boxes that Facilities will deliver on 10 November. Second, label every box with your name and team. Finally, save all your files on the shared drive, because our computers will be reset.

There will also be some changes in the new office. We will not have fixed desks any more, so you will need to book a desk using the new app. However, there will be four meeting rooms instead of one, and a much bigger kitchen.

If you have any questions, please let me know.

Best regards,
Claire

questionsOuvertesDebut.question: Please introduce yourself. Tell us your name, what you do, where you work and what you do on a typical working day.
questionsOuvertesDebut.reponseAttendue: Hello, my name is Karim Benali. I'm a sales assistant at Delta Home, a company that sells kitchen equipment. I work in our office in Lille. On a typical day, I start at half past eight. First, I read my emails and answer questions from customers. Then I prepare quotes and send them to our clients. In the afternoon, I often call customers to check their orders. I like my job because I speak to a lot of different people.

questionsOuvertesDebut.question: Some companies are asking employees to return to the office full-time, while others are keeping remote work. What is your opinion on remote work? Give reasons and examples to support your view.
questionsOuvertesDebut.reponseAttendue: In my view, a hybrid model is clearly the most effective option, although I don't think there's a single answer for every company. On the one hand, remote work has real advantages. People save time on commuting, and for tasks that need concentration, such as writing a report or analysing data, working from home is often more productive. In my previous job, our team actually completed projects faster after we introduced two remote days a week. On the other hand, full-time remote work has hidden costs. New employees learn a lot simply by listening to experienced colleagues, and that's much harder over video calls. Creativity also suffers: many good ideas come from informal conversations that never happen online. That said, forcing everyone back to the office five days a week sends a message of mistrust and may push talented people to leave. So I'd argue that the best approach is to agree on shared office days for collaboration and leave the rest flexible. What matters is not where people work, but whether the organisation of work is clear and fair.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: Your manager wants to replace the weekly team meeting with a short written update sent by email. Do you agree with this idea? Give your opinion and at least two reasons.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: In my view, a written update is useful, but it can't completely replace the weekly meeting. First, when we meet, we can solve problems immediately. If someone has a question about a client or a delivery, we answer it in two minutes, instead of sending ten emails. Also, the meeting is important for team spirit. New colleagues can ask questions and get to know the team. On the other hand, I agree that some meetings are too long. So I would suggest a compromise: a short email update on Monday, and a twenty-minute meeting on Thursday only for the important topics.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: In a team meeting, a colleague proposes closing the reception desk of your medical centre from 12 to 1 pm every day so that all receptionists can have lunch together. You disagree. Politely explain why and suggest an alternative.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: I see your point, and I agree that we all need a proper lunch break. However, I'm afraid I don't think closing the desk is the best solution. Many patients come at lunchtime because they work in the morning, and some of them arrive for appointments at half past twelve. If the desk is closed, they will have to wait outside, and we may receive complaints. What if we organised staggered breaks instead? For example, two receptionists could have lunch from twelve to half past twelve, and the other two from half past twelve to one. That way, the desk stays open and everyone still gets a break.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: In a meeting, your hotel manager says: 'We need to improve the check-in process before the summer, so I'd like a few ideas from the reception team soon.' The instruction is not clear to you. Ask at least two questions to clarify it, then rephrase what you have understood.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: Sorry, could I ask a couple of questions to make sure I understand? First, what do you mean by 'soon'? Do you need our ideas this week, or before the end of the month? And how would you like to receive them: by email, or should we present them at the next meeting? Also, is there a budget for new equipment, like a check-in tablet, or should our ideas be free of cost? So, if I understand correctly, you want each receptionist to suggest a few ideas to make check-in faster before the summer, and you'd like them by a date we'll agree on today. Is that right?

questionsOuvertesFin.question: You are the supervisor of the reception team at a medical centre. Tomorrow, a new online appointment booking system starts. Open a short team briefing: state the objective, explain how the briefing will be organised (two or three steps) and say clearly what you expect from each team member.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: Good morning, everyone, and thanks for coming. This briefing will take about ten minutes. As you know, our new online booking system starts tomorrow, so the purpose of this briefing is to make sure we are all ready on day one. First, I'll show you the three main screens of the system. Then, Amina will explain what to say to patients who still want to book by phone. Finally, we'll organise the first week. Now, my expectations. By the end of today, I need each of you to log in once and check that your password works. Tomorrow, Amina and Joe will start at eight to help patients at the self-service screen, and the others will start at the usual time. If a patient has a problem, please note it in the shared file, and we'll review all the problems together on Friday. Any questions? OK, let's wrap up. Thanks, everyone.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: You are chairing a 15-minute meeting at Lindenbrook Logistics about reducing late deliveries. Open the meeting (aim, agenda, timing), invite one colleague to present an idea, react briefly, and then close the meeting by summarising the decision, who is responsible and the next date.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: Good morning, everyone, and thanks for joining. Let's get started, because we only have fifteen minutes. The aim of this meeting is to agree on one simple action to reduce late deliveries, which went up by nine per cent this quarter. There are three items on the agenda. First, Amira will present her idea. Then, we'll discuss it together. Finally, we'll decide who does what. Amira, would you like to start? … Thank you, Amira. So, if I understand correctly, you suggest loading the trucks thirty minutes earlier. Tom, what do you think? … That's a fair point about the staff. What if we only tested it on the two longest routes? … Good, I think we agree. Let's sum up. We'll test earlier loading on two routes for two weeks, starting next Monday. Tom will collect the delivery times every Friday, and Amira will find volunteers in the loading team. We'll review the results on the fourteenth. Does anyone have any other business? No? As requested, here is a short review of our first participation in the Outdoor Trade Fair in Munich last week.

Our stand was in a good location near the main entrance, so we had a lot of visitors. In total, we collected 140 contacts, including 25 potential distributors. Marketing Assistant

exercices.reponseAttendue: In my view, a written update is useful, but it can't completely replace the weekly meeting. First, when we meet, we can solve problems immediately. exercices.reponseAttendue: I see your point, and I agree that we all need a proper lunch break. However, I'm afraid I don't think closing the desk is the best solution. Many patients come at lunchtime because they work in the morning, and some of them arrive for appointments at half past twelve. If the desk is closed, they will have to wait outside, and we may receive complaints. What if we organised staggered breaks instead? For example, two receptionists could have lunch from twelve to half past twelve, and the other two from half past twelve to one. That way, the desk stays open and everyone still gets a break.

In a meeting, your hotel manager says: 'We need to improve the check-in process before the summer, so I'd like a few ideas from the reception team soon.' The instruction is not clear to you. Ask at least two questions to clarify it, then rephrase what you have understood.

exercices.reponseAttendue: Sorry, could I ask a couple of questions to make sure I understand? First, what do you mean by 'soon'? Do you need our ideas this week, or before the end of the month? And how would you like to receive them: by email, or should we present them at the next meeting? Also, is there a budget for new equipment, like a check-in tablet, or should our ideas be free of cost? So, if I understand correctly, you want each receptionist to suggest a few ideas to make check-in faster before the summer, and you'd like them by a date we'll agree on today. Is that right?

As you know, our new online booking system starts tomorrow, so the purpose of this briefing is to make sure we are all ready on day one. First, I'll show you the three main screens of the system. Then, Amina will explain what to say to patients who still want to book by phone. Finally, we'll organise the first week. Now, my expectations. By the end of today, I need each of you to log in once and check that your password works. Tomorrow, Amina and Joe will start at eight to help patients at the self-service screen, and the others will start at the usual time. If a patient has a problem, please note it in the shared file, and we'll review all the problems together on Friday. Any questions? OK, let's wrap up. Thanks, everyone.

The aim of this meeting is to agree on one simple action to reduce late deliveries, which went up by nine per cent this quarter. There are three items on the agenda. So, if I understand correctly, you suggest loading the trucks thirty minutes earlier. Tom, what do you think? … That's a fair point about the staff. What if we only tested it on the two longest routes? … Good, I think we agree. Let's sum up. We'll test earlier loading on two routes for two weeks, starting next Monday. From: Tomasz Wolny, Account Manager, Greenfold Packaging
To: Joy Abara, Purchasing Department, Alder & Finch Cosmetics
Subject: Changes to our prices from 1 January

Dear Ms Abara,

I am writing to let you know that, due to the sharp rise in the cost of recycled cardboard this year, we will have to increase the price of our standard boxes by 6% from 1 January.

However, as a long-standing customer, you can still benefit from the current prices on any order placed before 15 December, even if the delivery is scheduled for January or February.

I would also like to suggest a short call to discuss our new lightweight box, which uses 20% less material and could reduce the impact of the increase on your budget.

Please let me know when you are available next week.

Kind regards,
Tomasz Wolny
1. Why is Greenfold Packaging increasing its prices?
A. Transport costs have risen
B. A raw material has become more expensive
C. A new tax on packaging has been introduced
D. It is launching a new product
2. How can Ms Abara avoid the price increase?
A. By placing her order before 15 December
B. By accepting delivery before January
C. By paying in advance
D. By ordering more than usual
3. What does Tomasz propose?
A. A visit to the factory
B. A discount on all boxes ordered before January
C. A call about a new product
D. A meeting in January
exercices.reponseAttendue:
1. B — A raw material has become more expensive. « due to the sharp rise in the cost of recycled cardboard » : le carton recyclé est une matière première. Le nouveau produit est mentionné plus loin, mais n'est pas la cause de la hausse.
2. A — By placing her order before 15 December. « any order placed before 15 December, even if the delivery is scheduled for January » : c'est la date de commande qui compte, pas la date de livraison. D'où le piège de la deuxième option.
3. C — A call about a new product. « suggest a short call to discuss our new lightweight box » = un appel pour présenter un produit de remplacement. Aucune remise n'est proposée.

exercices.consigne:
Your company is thinking of replacing all internal face-to-face meetings with video calls. Do you think this is a good idea? Give your opinion and explain your reasons.
Préparation 45 s, réponse orale de 90 s.
Critères : Opinion exprimée clairement dès le début. ; Au moins deux arguments justifiés et un exemple concret. ; Nuance : une limite ou une concession (however, on the other hand). ; Temps de parole : au moins 72 secondes sur 90. ; Connecteurs oraux variés et discours fluide. ; Respect du sujet (réunions internes, pas les réunions clients)..
exercices.reponseAttendue: In my opinion, replacing some internal meetings with video calls is a good idea, but replacing all of them would be a mistake. First, video calls save a lot of time. In my company, colleagues work on three different sites, so a one-hour meeting often meant two hours of travel. With video calls, we can meet more often and for shorter periods. Second, it's cheaper and better for the environment, because people don't need to drive or take the train. However, some meetings really work better face-to-face. For example, when we start a new project or when there's a conflict in the team, it's much easier to understand each other in the same room. People are also more relaxed and creative. So, overall, I would suggest a mix: video calls for regular updates and short meetings, and face-to-face meetings once a month for important discussions and team building.

Subject: Proposal for our team-building day

Dear Sarah,

Following our discussion at the last team meeting, I would like to propose an activity for our team-building day next spring.

My suggestion is a cooking workshop at Saltmarsh Kitchen Studio, which is about twenty minutes from the office. The workshop is designed for groups of up to 24 people. Participants work in small teams to prepare a three-course lunch, and then everyone eats together. The best date would be Friday 17 April, as there are no major deadlines that week.

I think this activity would be useful for several reasons. First, people from different units would work together, which is rare in our daily work. In addition, the teams have to plan, share tasks and manage time, so it is a good way to improve communication. Finally, it is a relaxed activity that everyone can enjoy, even people who do not like sport.

The total cost would be around €1,800, including the lunch and transport by minibus.

Could you let me know by the end of the month if you agree, so that I can book the studio?

Best regards,
Julia

reglementaire.titre: Fiche RS6905 – VTest Business English – 4 Skills (certificateur EXASSESS)
reglementaire.commentaire: Enregistrement au Répertoire spécifique le 28/11/2024 pour 3 ans (échéance 28/11/2027, dernière délivrance possible le 27/05/2028). La fiche décrit les 4 compétences évaluées (C1 à C4) et les niveaux A2 à C1 ; le niveau A2 est requis pour valider la certification.
reglementaire.exploitation: Preuve : fiche consultée et archivée dans le dossier qualité. Action : programmes, test de positionnement et livret d'accueil alignés sur les 4 compétences et sur le prérequis A2 à la validation.

reglementaire.titre: Décret n° 2024-394 du 29 avril 2024 relatif à la participation obligatoire du titulaire d’un compte personnel de formation
reglementaire.commentaire: Depuis le 2 mai 2024, le titulaire d'un CPF acquitte une participation forfaitaire lors de l'achat d'une formation, sauf cas d'exonération (demandeurs d'emploi, abondement employeur…).
reglementaire.exploitation: Preuve : décret archivé. Action : information du stagiaire sur le reste à charge lors de l'entretien d'entrée et dans les conditions générales de vente.

reglementaire.titre: Loi n° 2018-771 du 5 septembre 2018 pour la liberté de choisir son avenir professionnel
reglementaire.commentaire: La loi fonde l'éligibilité au CPF des certifications enregistrées au RNCP ou au Répertoire spécifique et l'obligation de certification qualité des organismes financés sur fonds publics ou mutualisés.
reglementaire.exploitation: Preuve : texte archivé. Action : vérification annuelle de la validité de l'enregistrement RS6905 avant toute ouverture de session financée par le CPF.

metier.titre: Cadre européen commun de référence pour les langues (CECRL) et son volume complémentaire
metier.commentaire: Le volume complémentaire du CECRL actualise les descripteurs (médiation, interaction en ligne, compétences plurilingues). Le VTest affine l'échelle en 10 niveaux de A2 à C1.
metier.exploitation: Preuve : descripteurs utilisés dans la grille de positionnement. Action : objectifs de chaque parcours rédigés avec les descripteurs du niveau visé.

metier.titre: Espace candidat VTest – passage du test en ligne
metier.commentaire: Le test se passe en ligne : compréhension orale et écrite adaptatives, expression orale notée automatiquement, rédaction en 30 minutes avec un nombre minimal de mots selon le niveau (80, 150 ou 200 mots).
metier.exploitation: Preuve : description des épreuves reprise dans le livret stagiaire. Action : entraînements chronométrés au format des 4 épreuves en fin de parcours.

metier.titre: Répertoire spécifique : liste des organismes préparant à la certification RS6905
metier.commentaire: La fiche publie la liste des organismes préparant à la certification ; l'organisme vérifie son inscription et les conditions fixées par le certificateur.
metier.exploitation: Preuve : capture de la liste. Action : convention ou accord avec le certificateur tenu à jour dans le dossier qualité.

technologique.titre: Description des niveaux communs de référence du CECRL
technologique.commentaire: Les descripteurs « interaction en ligne » et « médiation » s'appliquent aux réunions à distance et aux échanges écrits instantanés, désormais courants en contexte professionnel.
technologique.exploitation: Preuve : grille d'entraînement à la visioconférence. Action : mises en situation de réunion en ligne intégrées aux classes virtuelles.

technologique.titre: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 – recommandation W3C
technologique.commentaire: Les ressources audio et vidéo de la plateforme doivent être accompagnées de transcriptions et de sous-titres pour rester accessibles.
technologique.exploitation: Preuve : transcriptions disponibles pour chaque dialogue et audio. Action : contrôle de la présence des transcriptions à chaque mise à jour des contenus.
